citations.claim: body crossed through wall x-range between steps 5 and 6, ending left of wall
body was right of wall one step before, so centre path crossed wall box
both steps are within wall y-range showing crossing through wall face
speed far exceeds wall thickness per step, enabling step-boundary tunneling

counterfactual.change: reduced dt from 0.02523 to 0.005 with all else identical; smaller per-step travel lets discrete wall collision be detected, so no tunneling occurs

explanation: Fast body (speed ~57) moves ~1.05 in x per dt=0.025 step, far more than 0.2-thick wall (x 2.6-2.8). Positions jump from x=3.24 (right of wall) at step 5 to x=2.19 (left of wall) at step 6 while y stays inside wall span, so the centre segment pierces the wall between sampled steps. Despite 48 integration substeps, wall collision is missed, indicating collision/CCD is evaluated only at step boundaries or fails for thin walls at high speed.

violation.detail: body centre moved through wall 0 between steps 5 and 6

vision_note: The red circle approaches the thin vertical wall from the right across steps 3 to 5, reaching its edge at step 5. In step 6 it appears on the opposite left side of the wall, having passed through without bouncing or stopping.
